html:
The great festival of Athena in Athens, enlarged in 566 BCE with athletic and musical contests held every four years. It lasted into the 3rd century CE.

The high point was a procession through the city to the Acropolis, carrying a new woven robe for the old wooden statue of Athena. Many scholars think the frieze of the Parthenon shows it. Around this came contests in running, wrestling, chariot racing, music and the recital of Homer's poems, plus team events open only to Athenians.

Winners received large jars full of olive oil from Athena's sacred trees. These Panathenaic amphorae were painted with Athena on one side and the winner's sport on the other, in black-figure style, long after painters had moved to red-figure for everything else.

The expansion came in the years when Pisistratus was rising to power, and he and his sons made the festival a show of Athenian pride, a rival to the Olympic Games.
sum: The great festival of Athena in Athens, enlarged in 566 BCE with athletic and musical contests held every four years. It lasted into the 3rd century CE.
